The low sales filter ensures that products with small expenditure shares
do not unduly influence the index results.\

# Low sales filter {#Lowsalesfilter-Lowsalesfilter}

Even if they seem to be similar at first sight, a low sales filter has a
different objective than a dumping filter. The low sales filter ensures
that products with small expenditure shares do not unduly influence the
index results. A commonly used low sales filter includes only those
articles sold in two subsequent months which fulfil the following
condition (Eurostat\'s HICP - [Practical Guide for Processing
Supermarket Scanner
Data](https://circabc.europa.eu/ui/group/7b031f10-ac19-4da3-a36f-58708a70133d/library/8e1333df-ca16-40fc-bc6a-1ce1be37247c/details)).

$$\frac{s_{i}^{t-1}+s_{i}^{t}}{2}>\frac{1}{nλ}$$

where s~i~^t^ is the expenditure share of product i in month t, n is the
number of considered products and λ a parameter which can be considered
as a cut-off value determining the total expenditure share that shall be
covered. Typically, λ is set equal to 1.25 which means that only those
of the most sold products will be considered which represent about 80%
of the expenditures in the periods that are compared to each other
(Eurostat - Practical Guide for Processing Supermarket Scanner Data).
Depending on factors such as the market structure or the product life
cycle, other values for λ might be better suited for various product
groups. However, the value for λ should be chosen with caution as Bialek
and Beręsewicz (2021) showed that the value for λ can considerably
affect the index results. Care should also be taken for sellers with
large product offerings since a substantial portion of their overall
sales may be excluded with a low sales filter.\

Applying low sales filter to weighted indexes may not be required since
these indices allow every article to enter the index calculation
according to its importance (in terms of turnover share) anyway.
Therefore, weighted indexes are not prone to overrepresent articles with
neglectable turnovers. Nevertheless, in order to save computation time,
it might be helpful to use low sales filter also for weighted indices as
they remove products before the more computational expensive index
methods are applied. However, it should be investigated in advance
whether the results with and without low sales filters are comparable.
